newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu to leave hospital Thursday, plane stands by.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu to leave hospital Thursday, plane stands by.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, facing a Tutsi rebellion at home, will leave hospital in Monaco on Thursday after follow-up treatment for prostate cancer, a presidential spokesman said on Wednesday.
Airport officials in Nice said the 66-year-old president's private plane arrived on Tuesday night and was standing by to take him back to his war-torn country.

Mobutu's planned release from the Princess Grace hospital and the plane's arrival were the clearest signs yet that the veteran strongman aims to return to Zaire and make a stand against Tutsi rebels sweeping across the east of the country.
No date has been set for a departure.
Mobutu was admitted to the Monaco hospital at the weekend after a month convalescing in his nearby Riviera mansion from prostate surgery in Switzerland last August.

Mobutu's son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga has repeatedly said that his father, in power for almost 32 years, aims to return soon to Zaire in a bid to rally ragged government troops against the Tutsi rebels, led by Laurent Kabila.
Mobutu's white Boeing 727 and a cargo plane for his belongings were both waiting at the Riviera airport.
Meanwhile, France expressed worry on Wednesday over events in Zaire, a former Belgian colony, and said it was taking measures to protect its citizens.
"The current uncertainties have led us to take the necessary measures concerning the security of our citizens," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said at a regular briefing.
"We are in close communication with our European and American partners," he added. He gave no further details.
Rummelhardt said the attempt on Tuesday by Zaire's parliamentary opposition to oust Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, was a particular concern.
Kengo is in Kenya where African leaders opened a meeting in Nairobi on Wednesday on the Zaire crisis with a strong call for negotiations to end the war tearing apart the country.
Mobutu has spent most of his time in Europe since his cancer surgery. His departure has repeatedly been announced as imminent by his entourage, only to be delayed for medical reasons.

Mobutu Nzanga has repeatedly denied reports that his father is in serious condition, saying such reports were part of a political manipulation to oust him. He said on Tuesday his father was able to walk unaided in his hospital room.
The Congolese Red Cross said on Tuesday that members of Mobutu's family had taken refuge across the Zaire river in neighbouring Congo in the face of advances by the rebels.
